name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -21 point partisan lean
Incumbent David Taylor running with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger has raised only about $1,000
Prediction markets price Republican win at about 98%
model.rationale: The district's -21 point Republican lean, an incumbent with over $1 million raised, and a Democratic challenger with negligible funding all point to a decisive Republican win, and markets agree at roughly 98%. No polls or expert ratings contradict this picture.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or an unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This southern Ohio seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the state, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent David Taylor is running for reelection and has raised more than $1 million, leaving him with roughly $443,000 on hand. His Democratic challenger, Jennifer Mazzuckelli, has reported only about $1,000 raised and $219 on hand, giving her virtually no resources to compete.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available, but prediction markets price a Republican win at about 98 percent. With the incumbent advantaged on fundamentals, money, and geography, the race is rated Safe Republican, with Taylor expected to win by a wide double-digit margin.
